small_guidance:
- The inner loop redundantly reloads input pixels: for a given (kh,kw) and pool window, each ih=base_oh+dy+kh overlaps heavily across kh values. Restructure so the input gather over the (POOL+KH-1)×(POOL+KW-1) tile is loaded once per (ic, pool-window) and reused across all (kh,kw) — this cuts memory traffic ~KH*KW=9x.
- Sweep autotune configs: try OC_BLOCK ∈ {16,32,64}, P_BLOCK ∈ {64,128,256}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}. With OC=64, OC_BLOCK=64 (single oc tile, no atomic contention across oc) is likely best.
- Replace `tl.atomic_add(out_ptr + pid_n, s)` per (oc,p) tile with a per-(n, oc_tile, p_tile) write into a workspace then a final reduce, or have only one program per n accumulate locally — atomics across N*n_oc*n_p programs serialize the sum.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style direct conv where each program owns one (n, oc_tile, pooled-spatial tile) and persistently accumulates the full pool×kernel input patch in registers/SMEM: load a (POOL+KH-1)×(POOL+KW-1) input tile per ic once, then do KH*KW MACs against it for every dy,dx — this is the natural fusion of conv+avgpool and eliminates the 9x redundant input loads.
- Make the kernel persistent over OC so a single program per (n, p_tile) accumulates sigmoid-then-sum locally (no atomics, no workspace). Final result is one scalar per n via a single tl.sum across the OC×P tile, written non-atomically (one program per n owns disjoint p tiles, then atomic_add only across p tiles — far fewer atomics).
- Use channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the ic loop is the contiguous axis and loads coalesce; preload weight (small: OC*IC*KH*KW = 64*8*9 = 4608 floats) into SMEM once per program.
